newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate inches up to 10.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate inches up to 10.4 pct.

text.p: The average price of money on Croatia's money market inched up to 10.4 percent on Friday on shorter supply from 10.3 percent, but most rates were flat.
Dealers put the daily trade volume at 34.1 million kuna while banks sought 40 million to stock up for the week-end.
They said interbank rates ranged from 10 percent for call money borrowings to between 12 and 15 percent for term loans. Insurers rolled over their placements at 9.0 percent.
Only 12.7 million kuna were traded overnight on Thursday as one bank borrowed money to square position and others sought to keep their mandatory reserve requirement.
The central bank's exchange rates eased slightly to 5.3466 to the dollar while firming to 3.5649 versus the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
